messages:
anna: Heads-up — after the runtime change last night (kernel selector tweak + batching heuristic), we're seeing a ~12% increase in per-token tail latency on streaming routes. Per-route KPI for /v1/stream-chat shows token-level p99 spiking to ~220ms.
marco: Can you drop the dashboard link + quick repro steps? Which rollout touched selector/heuristics?
anna: Dashboard (mock): https://console/redwood/dashboard/perf?route=/v1/stream-chat
anna: Repro: curl the streaming endpoint with a long-context prompt (seq_len ~1024) and watch token waterfall. Happens consistently in production traffic during peak.
liam: perf-ci: uploaded kernel profile: s3://perf/profiles/1775122/profile-kernel-1775123000.pb.gz
anna: Quick find from the profile: kernel selection flipped to generic_cuda_fallback for ~18% of invocations for that model; previously optimized_int8 was dominant.
ingrid: That would explain longer kernel_exec times. Did model metadata or selector rules change?
anna: Yes — the selector rule tweak last night allowed fallback when est_seq_len > 768 OR when batch_size < 2. Also note we lowered min_batch_ms from 10ms -> 5ms to reduce latency for tiny batches; side-effect: more small batches and different kernel picks.
noah: Any KV cache signals? Could evictions / misses be contributing?
anna: KV hit rate for this route jumped down: baseline ~98% -> now ~91% during windows. Eviction spikes line up with the latency spikes (see top-left of dashboard). Likely working set thrash across shards after an autoscale/rebalance.
marco: Are stalls client-side or server compute? Where in the token timeline is the added time?
anna: Token-level waterfall shows server-side kernel_exec spike at around the 3rd chunk. Sample normal trace: ```enqueue 6ms -> batch_wait 4ms -> kernel_exec 45ms -> network_send 10ms```. Bad trace: ```enqueue 8ms -> batch_wait 6ms -> kernel_exec 140ms -> network_send 12ms```. So the kernel_exec part balloons.
ingrid: Sounds like fallback kernel is much slower for those shapes. Any canary where kernel was pinned?
anna: Yes — a 1% pinned optimized_int8 canary had no regression. Suggest interim fix: pin kernel selector to optimized_int8 for that model and revert min_batch_ms change to 10ms.
marco: We should add automated observability so this doesn't slip. Ideas?
anna: Proposal for metrics + dashboard tiles: streaming_chunk_gap_p50/p95, token_latency_by_stage (enqueue,batch_wait,kernel_exec,network_send), per_route_kv_hit_rate, kernel_selector_histogram, and per-route token-p95 baseline comparisons. Also an alert: token_latency_p95 delta > 20% vs baseline for 10m.
noah: Plan: 5% canary with kernel pinned + batching heuristic rollback for 30m, watch token-stage waterfall + kv hit rate + p95. Who owns?
anna: I'll own the canary and PRs for selector revert + dashboard widgets. I'll post the PR shortly. @perf-ci can you create the alert ticket and wire the dashboard tiles?
perf-ci: Created issue #512: "streaming token-stage alert + kernel-selector histogram". ETA for dashboard updates: ~2h.
ingrid: :thumbsup: nice triage. Keep us posted if canary is green or we see other regressions.
marco: If canary looks good, we'll roll to 25% then 100% with a rollback window. Also add a short-runbook note explaining kernel pin tradeoffs.
anna: Agreed — I'll add runbook section and include the perf profile link.
noah: Thanks, team.
